To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
smoking during pregnancy and breastfeeding are associated with child risk of asthma, eczematous dermatitis and allergy.
the risk of allergy among the offspring is higher when the mother has been smoking during pregnancy.
the risk of child allergy is higher among children of mothers smoking during pregnancy and breastfed <12 month, and children with eczemea are predisposed of having allergy and asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between the lifestyle of the Greenlandic mother, her diet, and the risk of asthma and allergy among children.
the relation between POPs and the risk for asthma, allergy and atopic dermatitis in children.
the effects of climate change, environmental pollution, and dietary transition on the health of the Greenlandic Inuit people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
smoking during pregnancy and breastfeeding for less than one year may predispose to allergy.
smoking during pregnancy and breastfeeding are associated with the risk of child allergy and asthma, but not with the risk of eczema.
breastfeeding is a risk factor for allergy and asthma, and that breastfeeding is a protective factor against asthma, and that smoking is a risk factor against asthma, allergy and atopic eczema.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Greenlandic women´s lifestyle (smoking) and diet (breastfeeding) during pregnancy may influence the risk of asthma and eczema in their children.
smoking during pregnancy increases the risk of allergy and that breastfeeding >12 months protects against asthma.
the risk of allergy among the offspring is higher when the mother has smoked during pregnancy and the offspring is breastfed <12months.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of child allergy was higher when the mothers were smoking during pregnancy, but the risk was lower when breastfeeding was prolonged.
the risk for child asthma, allergy, and eczema is increased when the mother smokes during pregnancy.
we have found an association between smoking during pregnancy, breastfeeding, and the risk of developing asthma, allergy and/or eczema in the child.
